newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed sues WorldCom over pact.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed sues WorldCom over pact.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp sued WorldCom Inc's MFS Technologies Inc unit and Delaware's Department of Transportation, seeking to overturn a $500 million contract for an electronic toll collection system awarded to MFS by the New Jersey Turnpike Authority.

In papers filed March 26 in the Delaware Chancery Court and released Monday, Lockheed alleged that the contract procurement process was "flawed," in part because a requirement for a revenue-generating fiber optic option was introduced late in the bidding process.

"This last minute change -- approved by a New Jersey official, Frank J. Wilson, was made not only long after the bids had been completely formulated...(but) far too late for Lockheed Martin to submit a bid responsive to the newly imposed criteria," court papers say.

Lockheed spokesman Terry Lynam alleged to Reuters that the process "was tainted by former transportation commissioner (Frank Wilson) who continued to stay involved in the procurement process even after he recused himself from further involvement because he was in job discussions with subcontractors of Lockheed and MFS."
MFS vice president of marketing, Bill Brogdon, told Reuters "All of those allegations have been made before and found to be totally unfounded.
"There was a 44 page ruling after an exceedingly fair and thorough review of (Lockheed's protest to the New Jersey ETC Consortium)...and the hearing officer found Lockheed's allegations baseless."

"This is the largest procurement of its type anywhere and Lockheed is merely trying to preserve a business opportunity for their benefit. But we're moving along with business as usual. We are at a point where we need to negotiate a contract of terms and conditions with the consortium. We believe Lockheed's mission is to delay this...but we're interested in moving forward quickly," Brogdon said.

Lynam said Lockheed filed a second protest last week, this time with the New Jersey Transportation Authority. "If they reject the protest, as we expect, we will file in the appellate court in New Jersey," Lynam said.
In its lawsuit, Lockheed seeks to have the contract declared invalid and blocked from being executed.

The Delaware Department of Transportation was sued because it had "impermissibly and improperly" delegated its authority to the New Jersey agency and failed to solicit qualified bidders and proposals in accordance with the Delaware code, court papers allege.
Lynam said the Delaware Department of Transportation plans to extend the New Jersey toll system into Delaware, and based on the award, MFS would be doing some work in Delaware.
Delaware Secretary of State Ed Freel said he could not comment at this time.
